The host was then compared against the checked-out form per A3.
determinism.observed: md5 of the served RESPONSE BODY, the page on the host's disk and the release checkout all read 0d828b51d433a24f7e2ef2e6ea7967ee at 48,235 bytes with 344 CRLFs. The blob reads 3bbd5ab2 at 47,891 bytes -- a 344-byte delta exactly equal to the CRLF count, so the two forms differ by the line terminators and nothing else.

surprises: NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S132: the first deploy refused because a SPARSE release worktree cannot run deploy-to-ec2.sh -- the script resolves two .env S3 roots through lib/opal_naming.py address() (LGIC R30 forbids typing an address), address() loads all 7 files in infra/logic/registry/, and those were in the release commit but outside the cone. FileNotFoundError in Step 2/3, before any artifact was built or uploaded, so nothing was half-landed and the manifest was untouched. Fixed by widening the cone; HEAD did not move and the A1 guard and the page's checked-out md5 were both re-read afterwards. Same class as cloud-ops trap (4) for safe-apply, on the deploy path, which that trap does not name -- and `lib` was already in the cone, so the two roots are not interchangeable. Disposition UNDER_INVESTIGATION: the instance is resolved, the standing question (should release orders require infra/logic in the cone?) is the issuer's.

NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S120 (pre-existing, not mine to disarm): runbook 7.2 still named 7c558b4e21 as live although bacec95ccd had been deployed by another seat at 15:43Z. This order's standing clause made me rewrite that paragraph, so the gap the row names is closed as a side effect -- but the row's disarm_owner is the mcportal applier and I have not touched its state.

declared_exclusions.reason: The three gate arms are driven through the installed handler with _viewer stubbed per arm -- the stand-in the order names in step 5. What that does NOT exercise is the ALB authenticate-oidc default action plus identity.py, which is what turns a browser into a verified email. That half is exercised here only by the unauthenticated public GET (302 to Entra), which proves the wall is in front of the route but not that it resolves a real identity correctly; this release changes neither, and a real Opal employee opening the page is the CRO's confirmation, requested by message.

declared_exclusions.item: the audit record the admitted read would have written
declared_exclusions.reason: audit.log_call -> _emit -> put_object whenever AUDIT_S3_BUCKET is set, and this order's BOUNDS say no object is written to any bucket, so the harness replaced the sink with an in-process recorder. The verdicts are therefore MEASURED as what the sink would have received (ok / denied+roster) and NOT as objects in the audit bucket. Deliberate: the alternative was to breach the bound this very act is proving.

declared_exclusions.item: whether the harness upload itself is inside the no-object bound
declared_exclusions.reason: Rule 12 forbids inlining a diagnostic script into an SSM command, so the harness reached the host as one object in the code-artifact store that the deploy had itself just written two objects to. I read the bound as being about data and served-output buckets, not the code-artifact store that is the deploy mechanism -- otherwise step 4's own deploy would breach it. Named rather than assumed; the issuer's to settle.
